assessments.reasoning: The official annotated SPDX Data object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The Canadian detail URL uses that target. GitHub records the tag as unsigned.

The pinned detail gives licenseId OGL-Canada-2.0, name Open Government Licence - Canada and isDeprecatedLicenseId false. crossRef and seeAlso give https://open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada. The plain-text Versioning clause supplies the edition omitted from the display name.

The English government original directly confirms the referred-to Canadian v2.0 edition at [17577,17638). Its provider definition documents the wording difference. This is contextual evidence for the destination of the SPDX mapping, whose assignment belongs to SPDX.

challenge.method: Compared the tag target with the generated detail revision, tested UK v2.0 as a competing identifier, and checked the Canadian reference fields against the English retrieval URL, canonical link, French alternate and Versioning paragraph. Compared licenseText with the monarch template and live definition.
challenge.results: Both SPDX references give the inspected HTTPS English URL. The publisher’s canonical metadata uses HTTP on the same host and path. The French alternate has a different path. Canada-specific law, provider and version exclude UK v2.0. SPDX licenseText says “Her Majesty the Queen,” the live definition says “His Majesty the King,” and the SPDX template’s monarch variable permits either. This accounts for a recorded match of “true” being compatible with different literal wording.

limitations: The unversioned government URL can change. A future capture requires a new edition and representation check. The French text, XML build lineage, legal equivalence, approval and application to a specific work fall outside this correspondence.
reasoning: SPDX Data 3.29.0 assigns OGL-Canada-2.0 to a detail whose name omits the version. Both the detail’s licenseText and the linked English government page expressly declare Canadian version 2.0. Checking those declarations satisfies the SCES §3 requirement to establish the edition independently of a moving URL. The tag target supplies the exact owning-index revision required by §7.
